content: The L1 family consists of a group of cell adhesion molecules that include various L1-like proteins. These proteins are present in the nervous system as well as in other tissues across numerous animal species. They are specifically located on radial glial cells, where they play a critical role in facilitating neural cell migration during developmental processes. In humans, the members of the L1 family include L1, CHL1 (Close Homolog of L1), Neurofascin, and NrCAM (NgCAM-related Cell Adhesion Molecule). A defining characteristic of this family is their ability to interact with a group of proteins known as ankyrins. Both NrCAM and Neurofascin possess class 1 PDZ domain-binding motifs at their carboxy-terminal (COOH) ends. NrCAM, in particular, has the capacity to bind to SAP102 and other proteins within the MAGUK (Membrane-Associated Guanylate Kinase) family.
